overview: Both sides mirror with the bishop on its active diagonal. White continues 3.Nf3 Nc6 reaching a Giuoco Piano, or plays 3.c3 Nf6 4.d4 or 3.Qe2 (the Philidor-style set-up) aiming at a flexible centre. The position is symmetrical and quiet, with both sides developing and castling before deciding the centre; it transposes widely to the Italian.

white_ideas.idea: Nf3, c3 and d4 to build a centre like the Giuoco Piano
Qe2 and Nc3 with a flexible, solid set-up avoiding theory
Use f4 or Nf3 choice to avoid the Petrov and other heavy theory

black_ideas.idea: Mirror development with ...Nf6 and ...Nc6, castle and break with ...d5
Challenge the centre once White commits with c3 and d4 using ...exd4
Keep a solid structure and equalise easily

typical_structures.structure: Giuoco Piano or Pianissimo structure with e4/d3 against e5/d6

character.notes: Symmetrical, quiet development; lines transpose to Italian lines with no early risk for either side.

gambit.notes: No material is sacrificed in the main lines.

structure.notes: Centre in tension with d3 or d4 options, Italian-like, so Flexible.

approach.notes: A less common line that strong players use now and then.

level.notes: Simple development and transposition; easy to learn but needs the Italian ideas.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.c3 Nf6 4.d4
sublines_that_differ.how: Sharper, with an open centre and tactics like the Italian's Greco lines.

character.reason: Symmetrical and quiet without forcing play or fortress features.

approach.reason: Respectable and used by strong players now and then.

level.reason: Clear development but some transposition know-how.

plans.reason: Bishops aim at f7 and f2 in a mirrored set-up.
